description: Polls a Teams channel and launches a chat-agent asset for a mention or a reply in an already-answered thread -- identifiers only in run tags, never the message text.

teams_team_id.label: Teams Team Id
teams_team_id.description: Teams team id (Teams client -> team -> ... -> Get link).

teams_channel_id.label: Teams Channel Id
teams_channel_id.description: Teams channel id inside the team (e.g. '19:xxx@thread.tacv2').

asset_selection.label: Asset Selection
asset_selection.description: The agent asset (and anything downstream, e.g. a teams_reply asset) to materialize when a message matches: explicit key list, the Dagster selection DSL (tag:/group:/kind:/boolean composition), '*', or a bare fnmatch glob -- resolved against sibling assets in the same defs folder, same as teams_run_request_sensor's own asset_selection trigger.

oauth_state_dir.label: Oauth State Dir
oauth_state_dir.description: Local path or fsspec URI (s3://, gs://, abfs://) dedicated to this sensor's '.teams_oauth_state.json' -- holds a rotated OAuth refresh token, if Microsoft ever issues one. Without a durable place to persist it, the next rotation breaks this sensor's auth entirely.

teams_tenant_id_env_var.label: Teams Tenant Id Env Var
teams_tenant_id_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD tenant id.

teams_client_id_env_var.label: Teams Client Id Env Var
teams_client_id_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD app registration client id. Also the default source for bot_application_id when that field is left unset.

teams_client_secret_env_var.label: Teams Client Secret Env Var
teams_client_secret_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD app registration client secret.

teams_refresh_token_env_var.label: Teams Refresh Token Env Var
teams_refresh_token_env_var.description: Env var holding the INITIAL OAuth refresh token (one-time interactive consent for the dedicated bot account -- see README, 'Auth'). Only the seed; a later rotation is persisted to oauth_state_dir instead.

bot_application_id.label: Bot Application Id
bot_application_id.description: This bot's own Azure AD application (client) id, for mention-detection -- a message's mentions[] carries mentioned.application.id when a bot/app is @-mentioned (confirmed against Graph's own chatMessageMentionedIdentitySet schema). Defaults to reading teams_client_id_env_var's own value if unset, since there is no Teams equivalent of Slack's auth.test self-lookup under a delegated token (it represents the consenting HUMAN, not the bot identity) -- set this explicitly only if that assumption ever proves wrong for your tenant.

trigger_mode.label: Trigger Mode
trigger_mode.description: 'mention' (default): only a message that @-mentions the bot starts a NEW conversation (a reply in an already-tracked thread still matches regardless of mode -- see follow_up_threads). 'all' matches every new root message unconditionally -- never use this on a busy shared channel. Unlike slack_agent_request_sensor, there is no separate 'dm' mode: this sensor only polls team CHANNELS, never 1:1 personal chats, the same scope teams_run_request_sensor already has.

follow_up_threads.label: Follow Up Threads
follow_up_threads.description: Also launch a run for a NEW REPLY in a thread this sensor has already launched a run for -- not gated by trigger_mode. Unlike Slack, Graph's replies endpoint has no delta/incremental query (confirmed against Microsoft's own API reference), so this re-fetches and diffs ALL replies in each tracked thread every tick -- real, higher cost than the Slack version. Set false for a channel with many concurrent long-lived threads.

known_threads_limit.label: Known Threads Limit
known_threads_limit.description: Most-recently-active threads to keep polling for follow-ups. Bounds both cursor size and the extra replies-list calls follow_up_threads costs per tick.

resolve_requester_email.label: Resolve Requester Email
resolve_requester_email.description: Resolve the message sender's Azure AD object id to an email address (needs delegated User.Read.All) before setting the teams/user tag -- most owners: checks downstream (e.g. dagster_workflow_tools' launch_job) use emails, not Azure AD object ids. When false, teams/user carries the raw Azure AD object id instead.

messages_per_poll.label: Messages Per Poll
messages_per_poll.description: Messages/replies to request per Graph page (Graph's own hard cap is 50).

max_pages_per_poll.label: Max Pages Per Poll
max_pages_per_poll.description: Follow at most this many '@odata.nextLink' pages per poll, for both new-root-message and (per-thread) replies polling.

process_backlog_on_first_run.label: Process Backlog On First Run
process_backlog_on_first_run.description: If false (default), the first-ever tick seeds the cursor to 'now' and processes nothing -- activating this sensor never answers a channel's past history.

post_acknowledgement.label: Post Acknowledgement
post_acknowledgement.description: React to a matched message immediately (acknowledgement_reaction) so the sender sees it was received before the agent run even starts. Needs delegated ChannelMessage.Send (the same scope already provisioned for replies).

acknowledgement_reaction.label: Acknowledgement Reaction
acknowledgement_reaction.description: Reaction for post_acknowledgement -- any Unicode emoji character, or a legacy name ('like', 'heart', 'laugh', 'surprised', 'sad', 'angry').

set_isolation_disabled_tag.label: Set Isolation Disabled Tag
set_isolation_disabled_tag.description: Tag every RunRequest dagster/isolation: disabled, so the run starts in-process on the code location server instead of spinning up an isolated container (which can take up to 3 minutes on Dagster+ -- far too slow for chat). Needs non_isolated_runs enabled on the deployment, and a sensible max_concurrent_non_isolated_runs (default 1 on Dagster+ -- a second concurrent question falls back to a slow isolated run, not a queue, if you don't raise it).

use_in_process_executor.label: Use In Process Executor
use_in_process_executor.description: Tag every RunRequest with run_config={'execution': {'config': {'in_process': {}}}}, so the agent asset and its downstream teams_reply asset run as plain function calls in one step-process instead of each spawning its own multiprocess-executor subprocess. Requires the code location that owns these assets not to set a non-default executor itself -- if it does, this run_config key is rejected by that executor's own config schema and the run fails with a RunConfigValidationInvalid error. Set false to leave execution untouched.

minimum_interval_seconds.label: Minimum Interval Seconds
minimum_interval_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between sensor evaluations. Chat latency is roughly this plus the run-queue dequeue time plus the LLM call -- keep this low.

default_status.label: Default Status
default_status.description: 'RUNNING' or 'STOPPED' -- initial status of the sensor.

placeholder_text.label: Placeholder Text
placeholder_text.description: If set, post this text as a new reply right after acknowledging a matched message, and tag the run teams/placeholder_id with that reply's own id. teams_reply then edits THIS reply with the final answer (PATCH .../replies/{id}, delegated ChannelMessage.ReadWrite -- a DIFFERENT scope than ChannelMessage.Send, which only covers posting) instead of posting a new one, and its failure_watcher edits it with the error. Leave unset (default) to skip this -- teams_reply just posts new replies, as before.

skip_in_branch_deployments.label: Skip In Branch Deployments
skip_in_branch_deployments.description: Skip every tick while running inside a Dagster+ branch deployment (DAGSTER_CLOUD_IS_BRANCH_DEPLOYMENT=1). A branch deployment runs its own copy of every sensor alongside the full deployment's -- without this, a branch deployment double-acknowledges the same message and double-launches a run for it.
